A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MaterialMVP research. All 12 pages of each were inspected, including equations, figures, tables, and end matter. Both end with references; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations in Table 1, qualitative generation results, and ablations of the generation strategy, consistency loss, and Multi-Channel Aligned Attention.

after.justification: v2 retains the original quantitative evaluations in Table 1 and the qualitative, application, and ablation results in Figures 4–8.

M1.justification: Reference conditioning, consistency-regularized training, dual-channel generation, MCAA, and learnable material embeddings remain unchanged. Section 3 newly explains how normal and position maps enter the U-Net, documenting the existing geometry conditioning without establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use Objaverse and Objaverse-XL for training and an Objaverse subset for evaluation. The texture-generation tasks, qualitative object examples, material variations, and environmental-lighting scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains Text2Tex, SyncMVD, Paint-it, both conditioning modes of Paint3D, and TexGen. The qualitative comparisons retain their comparator sets, and SuperMat remains the two-stage comparator in the generation-strategy ablation.

E3.justification: The 176-object evaluation, metrics, 512 × 512 training renders, six-view training samples, and reported training settings are unchanged. Section 3.2.1 newly specifies that the three HDR lighting conditions are random; this clarifies a previously unspecified detail rather than replacing an explicitly stated setting.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Figure 8 retain the same one-stage versus two-stage comparison, consistency-loss removal, and MCAA replacement analyses. The material-diversity and relighting demonstrations are also retained without added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Table 1 continues to report point estimates only.

E6.justification: Table 1's values and rankings are identical, including MaterialMVP's FID of 168.5, CLIP-I of 0.9207, and LPIPS of 0.1211. Visual inspection confirms that the qualitative comparisons, application examples, and ablation results are retained.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, reference-pair sampling definitions, diffusion and consistency losses, and the weighting parameter remain unchanged. Neither version introduces additional assumptions, propositions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about one-stage PBR generation, illumination invariance, view consistency, material alignment, and superiority over existing methods.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations of semantic alignment, lighting behavior, two-stage error accumulation, excessive metallic predictions without consistency loss, and artifacts from material misalignment. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications are added.

D1.justification: Section 3 adds that normal and position maps are encoded into latent space and concatenated channel-wise with noise for U-Net input. Section 3.2.1 specifies random HDR lighting, and Figure 1 replaces the project-page pointer with an explicit results-and-code repository link. Repository availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Reframe, PSHuman, CMD, and Multi-view large reconstruction model via geometry-aware positional encoding and attention. The research positioning otherwise remains stable. FlexiTex is retained with updated publication information, rather than constituting a new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short implementation explanation and a funding acknowledgment, revises author affiliations, and supplies contact information. The section sequence and nearly all scientific prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with clearer geometry-input connections, several figures are resized, and figures and text are reflowed. Figure 7 moves from page 8 to page 7. All eight figures and Table 1 remain, with their substantive result content retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves reproducibility documentation by explaining geometry conditioning, specifying random HDR lighting, and providing an explicit code-access link. The revised overview diagram supports this clarification. These changes reduce implementation ambiguity, while the method, empirical evidence, and central claims remain unchanged; actual repository availability is not established by the PDFs.
